findings.reason: the test spec would build a state the resume cannot leave, so the first case would not be a faithful reproduction and the guard's absent-record arm (the one the real state exercises) would go untested.
findings.text: the done-when builds the first two cases with "whose worker record and pointer still name attempt 5's exited process", but the resume path `_prepare_attempt_records` (reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1621-1638) unlinks the canonical `worker.json` and `exit.json` in one loop before attempt 6's supervisor starts, so the measured state at 06:58:17–06:58:30 has the worker record ABSENT (the plan's own timeline has attempt 6's worker "register" only at 06:58:30Z); a test built to this spec does not reproduce the incident it cites, and the plan's earlier review already corrected exactly this mistake for the exit record while treating the worker record as surviving

findings.reason: the deliverable already states the requirement (past the bound it reads as a stranded launch), so the parenthetical "as today" is a wording imprecision a careful implementer resolves against the done-when, not a wrong mechanism.
findings.text: §27 asserts a run past the bound "reads as a stranded launch, as today", but `_stranded_launch` (reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:444-458) returns False whenever the pointer carries a pid, and the case §27 describes always carries attempt 5's pid, so the existing stranded path does not fire for it; the deferral must carry its own bound rather than delegate
